<reason>B wins a competitive debate by better distinguishing legitimate operational restrictions from reputation-only exclusion. A established meaningful business costs and brand-autonomy interests, but B answered the cost question directly, preserved exceptions for actual service failures, and explained why gateway access differs from retail endorsement. A’s property framing did not sufficiently answer B’s comparison between compliant creators’ livelihoods and platforms’ preference against association. B also sharpened the final clash, while A largely returned to its original entitlement objection.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B effectively challenged A’s conflation of reputational backlash with operational misconduct. After A defended excluding a safely gated app without evidence of likely financial loss, B clarified that freedom of contract identifies who decides—not why exclusion is justified.</best_rebuttal>
